#265: PASS WITH NOTES
Head: 9e665af8b04ef4fc03f309cfa8fb7d02211e3386
Base: dba0c080 (#263 merged)
Role: reviewer, instance 265

No blocking correctness findings.

The sibling regression now exercises the observed shape. registration.rs:3402-3456 gives each new process the original HOST parent; only HOST, SHELL and the current restart are alive. At 3483-3501, the complete returned descriptor is fed into the next registration, so proc actually advances through r1, r2 and r3 while anchor remains HOST. The earlier #263 fixture reset that state and could not establish transitivity; this one would fail under #263's rule.

Anchor lifecycle is sound for production-created routes. register_inner at 1207-1214 selects anchor.or(descriptor.proc) only on an existing proxied route and matches the exact ProcIdentity against verified native ancestry. It copies the selected anchor unchanged. Gate failure and opt-out use SeatCacheProxy::plain, which sets anchor=None (model.rs:618-624); a successful fresh gate also starts with anchor=None (cache_proxy.rs:269-274). Spawn/revive constructs a new descriptor and assigns that gate decision wholesale (http/mod.rs:1664-1674), not the displaced carried route. A non-descendant registration clears the complete cache_proxy option (registration.rs:1226-1227). Store upsert serializes the whole option and assigns cache_proxy=excluded.cache_proxy (registry.rs:595-624), so there is no separate retained anchor to resurrect a plain route. Same-process registration and /new appropriately preserve the still-proxied route and anchor.

Pre-anchor compatibility: serde(default) reads existing JSON without anchor. For an older gate stamp whose row.proc still identifies its stamped launch, using that verified proc as the initial anchor is correct; the sibling test starts with exactly anchor=None and establishes it on the first carry. A legacy #263 carried row is different: its row.proc is already r1 and its original supervisor was never stored. Its next sibling r2 cannot recover that supervisor and reads plain. pm-001 explicitly confirmed this is the accepted forward-only F221 won't-fix (display only; heals on revive), not upgrade recovery required by #265. This note also applies to rows whose route was already lost. No backfill or environment inspection is implied.

Guards checked read-only: pid-only matching fails a_reused_pid_carries_no_route for both absent and present anchors; dropping the lineage guard fails the outside-lineage test; ignoring/resetting the retained anchor fails the second sibling step and explicit anchor assertion; retaining a route/anchor on a plain transition fails the outside-lineage sequence, which tries the original supervisor again after clearing. The forged-claim test deserializes a cache_proxy plus anchor through the actual Registration type, then registers it and expects no route. Opt-out and fresh revive assertions remain explicit. I did not rerun the author's eight mutation builds.
